lines.opening: Hello, this is the automated assistant of Corrib Valley Bank. We record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I am the automated assistant of Corrib Valley Bank.
lines.scam: I understand your concern. You can check that this call is genuine by calling Corrib Valley Bank on the number on our website or in the app.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can explain the reason for my call once I have confirmed that I am speaking with the right person.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share any details on this call.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand. This will only take a few minutes.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach {first_name} {last_name}?
lines.tp_ask_time: What time would suit, today or on the next business day, between 9:30 in the morning and 6 in the evening?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, I can only arrange a call later today or on the next business day, between 9:30 in the morning and 6 in the evening. What time would suit?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can only discuss the reason for my call with {first_name} {last_name}.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you. We will call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: I'm sorry to have bothered you. Thank you for letting me know.
lines.condolence: I'm very sorry for your loss, and I apologise for the disturbance. Thank you for telling me.
lines.id_intro: Before we go on, I need to ask you two short security questions.
lines.id_why: We ask these questions to protect your information and to make sure we are speaking with the right person.
lines.id_explain: I can only continue once you have answered the security questions.
lines.id_declined: I understand. Without the security questions I can't continue this call. You can visit a branch or use the Corrib Valley Bank app.
lines.id_repeat: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that answer doesn't match.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I can't confirm your identity, so I can't go any further on this call. Please visit a branch or use the Corrib Valley Bank app.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you, {first_name}. I'm calling about overdue payments on your account.
lines.product_line: Your {name} has {amount} overdue and is {days} days past due.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full overdue amount of {amount} today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay the full overdue amount of {amount} on your {name} today?
lines.offer_floor_date: I understand. The lowest amount I can accept is {amount}. Could you pay that on {date}?
lines.offer_floor: I understand. The lowest amount I can accept is {amount}. Could you pay that?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {floor}. Could you pay {floor}?
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, that date has already passed. Which day from today onwards would work for you?
lines.not_business_day: That day is not a business day. The next business day is {date}. Would that work for you?
lines.after_deadline: I'm sorry, the latest date I can accept is {date}. Could you pay on that date?
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day would that be?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which day could you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: To repeat: could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.readback_intro: Let me read that back to you.
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the date is {date}, the latest date I can accept for it.
lines.recorded: Thank you, your promise has been recorded.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, your promise could not be recorded because of a system problem.
lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know. Payments can take up to two business days to show on your account.
lines.dispute_line: I understand, and I won't discuss this amount further on this call.
lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear that, and I'll put you through to our support team now.
lines.restructure_line: I'll put you through to our restructuring team, who can discuss that with you.
lines.human_ask_help: Is there something I can help you with myself?
lines.transfer: Please hold while I transfer you.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, I can't change a promise that has already been made on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't book the callback because of a system problem.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer did not go through.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I did not catch that. Do you confirm, yes or no?
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our systems are not responding at the moment, so I can't continue this call.
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {amount}.

quotes: A skipped step is not a proposal and does not count towards the limit; go straight to the next step.
This opening question is proposal 1 and counts towards the product's persuasion limit.
A step whose amount and date are both identical to a proposal already made for that product (the opening question included) is skipped.

rules.too_much_skips_full.assumption: The brief only says the next proposal after 'too much' is the floor. Later ladder steps naming the full amount are not skipped automatically, but never-repeat still applies.

quotes: "That is too much" means the next proposal you make is the floor.
rules.too_much_floor.derivation: The floor offer after 'too much' is a proposal, so it uses an attempt. The engine default attempt_1 is kept.

quotes: Stop proposing when the product's persuasion limit is reached or the ladder has no steps left, whichever comes first.
rules.ladder_repeat_last.derivation: When the ladder runs out, proposing stops, so the last step is not repeated.

quotes: Each flat refusal (a no with no date and no amount) moves to the next step of the ladder:
If `create_promise` fails twice, note `service_error` on that product.
rules.promise_retries.derivation: service_error is noted only after two failures, so a failed create_promise is retried once.

quotes: one sentence of sympathy, make no proposals, note `hardship` on each remaining product, then transfer the call straight away with `transfer_to_agent` queue `support`, without asking the customer first, and close `transferred` / `support`.
note `hardship` on each remaining product, then transfer the call straight away with `transfer_to_agent` queue `support`
rules.notes_before_transfer.derivation: In hardship, a hardship note is written for each remaining product before the direct transfer.

quotes: Only then, if the date you have is not a business day, move it forward to the next business day.
A customer who names a non-business day on or before the deadline is offered the next business day
For each product, the first thing the agent asks is: "Can you pay the full overdue amount of EUR {amount} today?"

rules.week_end_today.assumption: No ladder step uses the last business day of the week, so the rule has no effect.

quotes: overdraft: one quarter of `overdue_eur`, rounded up to the next whole euro (a whole-euro result stays as it is).

products.floor_min.assumption: There is no minimum floor beyond the overdraft rule for amounts below 100.

quotes: If `overdue_eur` is below 100, the floor is the whole overdue amount.
overdraft: one quarter of `overdue_eur`, rounded up to the next whole euro (a whole-euro result stays as it is).
half the overdue amount, rounded up to the next whole euro (a whole-euro result stays), on the deadline; if that is below the floor, the floor instead;
`create_promise` takes the amount in euro cents, as a whole number (EUR 45.10 is 4510).

products.promise_round.assumption: Euro amounts have at most two decimals, so multiplying by 100 already gives whole cents. No rounding rule is invented.

quotes: no promise recorded and at least one product refused (F.4), the rest disputed or paid
every product disputed (G.2)
G.6, or no promise recorded because of an F.5 failure
multi.outcome_priority.derivation: refused applies when at least one product is refused. dispute applies only when every product is disputed. service_error applies when the missing promise comes from an F.5 failure. When a failure is mixed with refusals, service_error is ranked first (the missing promise is due to the failure). A dispute/paid mix with no refusal is closed as dispute.

quotes: For calls made on or after 4 November 2026, the `close_call` reason `service_error` is replaced by `system_unavailable` (outcome stays `no_promise`).

assumptions: Memo OPS-26-31 overrides section H from 2026-11-04: the close_call reason service_error becomes system_unavailable (outcome no_promise). The add_note reason service_error does not change. The base event keeps service_error for calls before that date.
Verification ends at the second wrong answer across both questions (brief C.2). This overrides the API summary of three wrong answers, because the brief is more specific about agent behaviour.
The opening line the brief prescribes ('This call is recorded.') is spoken as 'We record this call.' to follow the spec's wording rule. The rest of the wording is kept.
In the first question, 'EUR {amount}' becomes '{amount}', because the engine already speaks the amount with the currency (euros).
B.1 gives no title variable, so confirm_ask uses {first_name} {last_name} as the brief says.

Products have a type field (kind: card/loan/overdraft). Card and loan floors come from min_due_eur and monthly_instalment_eur. The overdraft floor is 25% of overdue_eur rounded up to a whole euro (a whole result stays), or the whole debt when overdue_eur is below 100. Checks: 250.40 -> 62.60 -> 63; 400 -> 100; 100 -> 25; 80 -> 80.
Ladder step 2 is pct:50 rounded up to a whole euro (a whole result stays), then max(step, floor). Checks: 250.40 -> 125.20 -> 126; 300 -> 150.

opening_is_attempt is true, so ladder step 1 is the opening ask (full amount, today). Tier 1 (2 proposals) = opening + full on the deadline. Tier 2 (3 proposals) = opening + full on the deadline + half on the deadline. The floor step is reached only when a step was skipped as a repeat (for example, Tier 2 on the 15th, when the deadline is today).

Tier 1 deadline = the 6th business day after today, today not counted. Tier 2 deadline = the 15th of this month, rolled to next month's 15th only if it is before today. The non-business-day move forward comes after the roll (roll_before_adjust). When today is the 15th, the deadline is today.
deadline_adjust is next_business_day: D.3 moves a Tier 2 deadline forward, and D.4 offers the next business day for a non-business date the customer names.
The callback window is 09:30-18:00 inclusive, today or the next business day, and later than now. A second failed time ends with no_callback.
A spoken all-numeric date of birth is read day-month-year (date_order dmy) and sent as YYYY-MM-DD.

Hardship: one sentence of sympathy, a hardship note on each remaining product, a direct transfer to the support queue, and a close of transferred/support. The hardship event therefore uses outcome transferred and reason support.
Restructuring and human transfers write no notes. The brief requires notes only before the hardship transfer.
'If that is declined, treat it as a refusal' (the floor offered after a below-floor amount) is read as ending the product as refused, with a refused note.

The brief does not say: how 'next <weekday>' is read (default following_week); whether to ask 'anything else' after a promise (default yes); how many 'I don't want to talk' answers end the call (default 2); whether a promise can be changed (assumed it cannot be changed on this call); or a limit on unclear answers to payment questions (engine default).
Asking what the call is about instead of answering a security question counts as declining (engine default). The brief only says a refusing customer is told once why we ask.
Mixed closings with no promise: service_error (F.5 failure) is ranked above refused, then dispute, then paid. A dispute/paid mix with no refusal closes as dispute.
callback.business_days_only is false. The allowed days are 'today' and 'next_business_day', as B.2 states.
